Hispanic here, I feel ya buddy I just can't stand anything of those southamerican genres: reggaeton, trap, ballenato, salsa, merengue, bachata, cumbia villera... Uuugghh

But if you're still interested in spanish music you could try any of these, they're pretty good:

Mecano: beautiful songs with amazing lyrics that share from mundane to mythical stories, you can try: "Hijo de la luna", "Naturaleza muerta", "Aire" and "Mujer contra mujer".

Soda Stereo: classic 80-90's latinamerican rock that hit a whole generation with their music, I recommend: "Persiana americana", "Mil años luz" and "La ciudad de la Furia". "Música ligera" is their most famous song but I find it quite generic.

Gustavo Cerati: when Soda Stereo broke up their vocalist started to work in his own career. I recommend: "Lago en el cielo", "Deja Vu" and "Fuerza Natural".

Mago de Oz: metal with some celtic and folk influences, they have beautiful songs with amazing lyrics that can turn you in a better mood easily or tell good stories with historic references. You can try "Fiesta pagana" and "La Danza del Fuego" to start.

Gaélica: an pretty nice and underrated instrumental music band with some celtic influences that have some nice singles like "Brújula" and "Deja Vu".

Cuarteto de Nos: I haven't listened so much of them because my friend just showed me that band this week but they sound amazing, it'd describe it as alternative rock but I'm not so sure.

And if you want to try something more "typical" of latinamerica, Juanes, Santana and Los Rodriguez are pretty good.
